subject: Quick recap + next tests: hyperscaler SLA & incident escalation comparison
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@evergreen.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procure Team <procure@evergreen.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next tests: hyperscaler SLA & incident escalation comparison

Thanks for the demo this morning — good coverage. A few follow-ups from our side related to incident response and how you compare to hyperscalers (AWS/GCP/Azure) before we loop procurement: 

- Incident SLA & credits: can you summarize your SLA timelines for P0/P1/P2 and how credits are calculated for hosted vs dedicated vs private? Evergreen procurement needs the delta vs our current hyperscaler endpoints (they care about measurable time-to-recover and credit patterns).
- RCA cadence and artifacts: what is your standard RCA timeline after a Sev1 incident (ack window, internal RCA draft, final RCA delivery)? Do you provide post-mortem artifacts (logs, timeline, mitigations) and are any of those redacted for hosted customers?
- On-call escalation: we need the exact escalation path (first-level support, on-call SE, engineering pager) and expected response windows for each level. Hyperscalers give a named SRE contact for Dedicated; is that available for Redwood Dedicated or Private?
- Test requests: we want to run a short, controlled "induced failure" exercise to measure time-to-detect and time-to-recover. Can you support a 1-hour simulation (with pre-arranged rollback) and capture telemetry?

Attachments referenced in the call: Evergreen included a baseline SLA matrix we use internally. We'll share it if helpful. Also tagging procurement (procure@evergreen.ai) so they can flag must-haves.

If you can send a one-page comparison and a proposed test plan, we can schedule the procurement call next week.

—Liam
Principal Product Manager
Evergreen Analytics

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@evergreen.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next tests: hyperscaler SLA & incident escalation comparison

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the priorities from procurement. Quick answers and proposed next steps below so we stay aligned before the test: 

1) SLA and credits (high level):
   - Hosted API: P0 (system outage) — 15 min ack, 1 hour mitigation target; credits based on prorated monthly usage as % of impacted window.
   - Dedicated: P0 — 10 min ack, 45 min mitigation target; deeper isolation means smaller blast radius and higher credit cap.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): support contract with SLOs set per customer — typical 4-hour target for P0 depending on infra ownership; can include named SRE add-on.
   I'll attach a concise SLA matrix and a one-page delta vs AWS/GCP that highlights typical response windows and credit formulas.

2) RCA cadence and artifacts:
   - Ack timeline: initial incident ack within SLA window above.
   - Preliminary RCA: draft within 72 hours with timeline and immediate mitigations.
   - Final RCA: delivered within 14 calendar days with logs, timeline, root cause analysis, and remediation plan. For hosted customers we can provide redacted logs as needed; for Dedicated/Private we can provide raw artifacts subject to contract and access controls.

3) On-call/escalation path:
   - Level 1 Support (Support portal) — initial triage (SLA windows apply).
   - Level 2 — Sales Engineering (Rishi) loops in SE on-call for escalations within 30–60 min for P0/P1.
   - Level 3 — Eng Pager (rotational) for critical system issues; named SRE available for Dedicated/private as an add-on.

4) Test plan proposal:
   - Controlled 1-hour induced failure (rate-limiting + simulated node failure) during a low-traffic window.
   - Redwood will collect telemetry (latency/5xx/queue depth), runbook timestamps (detect/ack/mitigate/recover), and post-test RCA.
   - Proposed dates: Nov 18 or Nov 20 (UTC-friendly window).

Next steps: I'll attach the SLA matrix and a short escalation playbook (PDF). Rishi will own the test instrumentation and Stephanie will coordinate SRE availability for the window. If that works, can procurement confirm a preferred date and whether they need SOC 2 evidence pre-test?

Thanks — Neha
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@evergreen.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procure Team <procure@evergreen.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next tests: hyperscaler SLA & incident escalation comparison

On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 11:03 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the priorities from procurement. Quick answers and proposed next steps below so we stay aligned before the test: 
> ...

Thanks Neha — that summary helps. A couple clarifications from procurement's perspective: 

- Dedicated named SRE add-on: procurement asks for a sample contact-level commitment (can you provide a short MSA addendum template showing the named SRE scope / contact window?).
- Post-test evidence: we need raw (or minimally redacted) request traces for the induced failure and a timeline CSV for detect/ack/mitigate/recover. Is that possible for hosted without exposing other tenants?
- SOC 2 evidence: yes — we need a copy of the SOC 2 type II report or a vendor authority letter confirming scope.

Procurement is fine with Nov 18 at 09:00 PT provided Redwood can confirm instrumentation and a limited blast radius (we'll sign an agreed rollback/kill-switch doc). Adding our procurement contact so they can coordinate paperwork.

—Liam

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Evergreen test + procurement asks (actions & owners)

Team — internal summary and owners after Evergreen confirmed Nov 18 @ 09:00 PT. Please treat as action items: 

- Rishi: own instrumentation and data capture. Deliverables: request-trace CSV schema + confirm whether we can provide per-request traces for hosted (redacted) by EOD 2026-11-17. Attach: evergreen-hyperscaler-sla-matrix.xlsx for context.
- Stephanie: confirm SRE on-call coverage for Nov 18 and whether we can offer a named SRE add-on sample agreement. Deliverable: draft addendum for procurement by 2026-11-18 12:00 PT. Attach: rfc-escalation-playbook.pdf.
- Neha: coordinate procurement paperwork and provide SOC2 copy via secure link. I will produce the one-page comparison vs hyperscalers and a concise test-run checklist. Deliverable: one-pager + checklist by 2026-11-17 17:00 PT.

Notes: keep the test scoped (no real customer data), use synthetic traces, and prepare a rollback plan. We'll treat any RCA artifacts as an internal deliverable first, then share redacted versions with Evergreen according to their contract.

Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
